problemStatement.formal: For absolutely continuous F on [a,b], recover F(b)-F(a) as the integral of F' and connect the Lebesgue FTC to classical differentiability and monotone a.e. differentiability statements.
problemStatement.plain: Develops the Lebesgue-version bridge for the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. The file defines an `AbsolutelyContinuousOn` predicate, states the differentiability and integral directions of the Lebesgue FTC, connects them back to the classical FTC, and records monotone almost-everywhere differentiability.
whyMatters: The classical FTC is a pointwise theorem; the Lebesgue FTC explains the measure-theoretic version used in modern analysis.
Absolute continuity is the right regularity condition for recovering a function from its derivative almost everywhere.
This entry marks the boundary between what is already in Mathlib and what still needs deeper measure-theory infrastructure.

proven: Defines `AbsolutelyContinuousOn` for real-valued functions on intervals.
`classical_ftc_from_lebesgue` connects the Lebesgue FTC assumptions back to the classical endpoint identity.
`monotone_ae_differentiable` records the monotone-function differentiability bridge used by the file.
The file relates the entry to Vitali covering and Lebesgue density style infrastructure rather than treating FTC as only a calculus identity.
open: The current proof file still contains two axioms for the Lebesgue FTC directions and one explicit sorry for Cantor-function infrastructure, so this is evidence-aware metadata rather than a claim of a closed proof.
A fully axiom-free version would need more Mathlib support for absolute continuity, a.e. differentiability, and singular functions.
